description.narrative: The development objective of the Meghalaya Community-Led Landscapes Management Project for India is to strengthen community-led landscapes management in selected landscapes in the state of Meghalaya. There are three components. First component, Strengthening Knowledge and Capacity for Natural Resource Management (NRM) objective of this component is to enable the development, assimilation, analysis, and dissemination of knowledge and skills to improve landscape management within the state. This component will comprise the following subcomponents. a) promotion of traditional knowledge, grass-root innovations, and communication; b) training and capacity building; c) preparation of strategies, research, and development; and d) monitoring, learning, and reporting (IBRD Financing; Second component, Community-led landscape planning and implementation will support both planning and implementation of the landscape plans by communities in the selected very high/high priority areas. It has three sub-component, a) preparation of community landscape plans; b) implementation of community landscape plans and implementation support; and c) implementation Support to community landscape planning and implementation; Third component, project management and governance will support the strengthening of the institutional capacity and knowledge management of the project implementing entity, Meghalaya Basin Management Agency (MBMA), for the implementation and management of the project including, among others, (a) establishment of the State Project Management Unit (SPMU) within the MBMA and support to seven District Project Management Unit (DPMUs), including technical staff and consultants; (b) the incremental costs associated with implementation; (c) administrative support to 20 Block Project Management Unit (BPMUs); and (d) technical fiduciary and safeguards oversight and supervision of project activities in the field.
The project development objective is to strengthen community-led landscapes management in selected landscapes in the state of Meghalaya.

title.narrative: Forest area brought under management plans

comment.narrative:
Fully Achieved and Exceeded (123%). The project brought areas of forests under sustainable planning using the forest and biodiversity management and monitoring protocol developed through project support. This indicator supported use of scientifically tested protocols to plan and monitor the status of forest in terms of forest cover and tree health. It also introduced new institutional approaches for landscape management by widening the scope and scale of forest monitoring. Overall, 110,000 hectares were covered by project Forest Management Plans including 15,444 hectares under CNRM plans with the remainder under Payments for Ecosystem Services (PES), far exceeding the intermediate indicator target for ”Forest area brought under management plans of 12,585 hectares”.
Data Sources and Assessment: Verification of forest management plans, impact evaluation report, project M&E and annual progress reports.

title.narrative: Community NRM management plans prepared and approved by Village CNRM Committees and DPMU of MBMA that include financing from other central and state government sources available for NRM

comment.narrative: Fully Achieved (100%). This indicator is related to PDO#2 and PDO#3. It further captures convergence of government sources for NRM. The indicator recorded the VNRM plans were prepared and approved by VNRMCs and the State DPMU of MBMA and included convergence from the MGNERGA (from central) to 279 villages and support from the Stated to all 400 villages through project counter-part funding. Data Sources and Assessment: This indicator was assessed through – a) third-party audit reports on fiduciary processes and findings; b) third-party assessment of impact evaluation reporting

title.narrative: Share of villages supported with capacity-building package in NRM

comment.narrative:
Fully Achieved (100%). All 400 villages were supported with a capacity building package in NRM, as planned.This indicator reports the number of villages supported by the project for improving management of natural resources through a series of capacity building programs and trainings, covering key areas of SLM practices. All 400 villages were supported with a capacity building package in NRM, as planned. Project also reached out to other villages over and above project villages and covered almost the entire state.
Data Source and Assessment: Impact evaluation report and project progress reports.

title.narrative: Meghalaya Basin Management Agency functional as Agency of Excellence in community-led NRM

comment.narrative: Fully Achieved (100%). This indicator relates to all four PDO indicators and reflects on institutionalization of the project efforts to strengthen landscape management practices in the state and ascertain continuity of SLM practices. The fully functional CoE housed within MBMA is tasked to generate and share knowledge on NRM practices to interested stakeholders in the state. Data Source and Assessment: Government Notification on MBMA to act as CoE for community-led NRM activities.

title.narrative: Share of village-level NRM Plans under implementation according to agreed criteria.

comment.narrative: Fully Achieved (100%). This indicator measures the community engagement and confirms that the project followed a successful strategy of engaging beneficiary groups at each stage of preparation of community NRM plans and implementation. For each CNRMP, the VNRMC passed a resolution, signed a green charter of willingness to engage and with the support from VCFs, DPMU and SPMU prepared, and gat approved the VNRM plans (at project portal) and signed the Village Green Charter to adopt the same. The planning support is measured in form of investment made to bring and archive technical knowledge on NRM practices and VCF appointments to facilitate the science-based participatory planning process in all 400 project villages, in place a village-level a CNRM plan, and implemented. Data Sources and Assessment: 400 CNRMPs hosted at MBMA website (links are provided in Annex 6); Appointment and payment documents against used of services of 13,000 VCF; Knowledge workshops and training completed.

title.narrative: Share of target beneficiaries with rating "Satisfied" or above on process and impact of project interventions. (Disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: Achieved and Exceeded (126%). The indicator measures the scale at which people benefitted from project activities, covering increase in productivity of agriculture and allied activities, improved management of forest and other NRs (especially springs), and improved livelihood. This indicator measures the success of the efforts made by the project in reducing the unsustainable practices and enhancing the alternative income sources for the project beneficiaries and measures the proportion of direct beneficiaries that are female thus confirms the gender focus of the project. The third-party Impact Assessment Report on completion of the project found that 88 percent of the respondent (average of five districts surveyed) are highly satisfied with the project outcomes compared to the 70 percent target. Data Sources and Assessment: A third-party impact evaluation gathered actual data/evidence, analysis of the approved Annual Action Plans, annual progress reports, project household survey

title.narrative: Land area under sustainable landscape management practices

comment.narrative: Achieved and Exceeded (148%). This indicator measures the extent to which the sustainable landscape management (SLM) practices were scaled up within the targeted project landscapes and other additional landscapes under catalytic fund, innovation grant and payment of ecosystem services (PES). Sustainable landscape management (SLM) practices refer to a combination of at least two technologies and approaches to increase land quality and restore degraded lands for example, agronomic, vegetative, structural, and management measures that, applied as a combination, increase the connectivity between protected areas, forest land, rangeland, and agriculture. At closing, 46,704 hectares of land were under sustainable landscape management practices, above the 31,510- hectare target. Data Sources and Assessment: Direct beneficiary feedback obtained during implementation support missions, Annual progress reports and impact evaluation reports.

title.narrative: Village NRM Committees functioning with adequate fiduciary capacities, and capable of monitoring capacities to lead on landscapes management

comment.narrative: Fully Achieved (100%). The indicator measures improved capacity of the functioning Village NRM Committees (VNRMCs, one in each 400 project villages) in terms of planning, implementing and monitoring NRM activities, which was necessary to lead and sustain sustainable landscape management practices. The functioning of the VNRMC could be demonstrated through adoption of the Green Charter and monetary and labor contribution by the community to implement planned CNRMP during and beyond project period. The fiduciary capacity is the measure of ability of the VNRM committees in bookkeeping, record keeping, and financial discipline followed in procurement of goods and services as well as maintaining accounts. At closing, 400 new VNRMCs were functioning with strengthened fiduciary capacity, as planned. Data Sources and Assessment: This indicator was assessed through – a third-party (a) audit reports on fiduciary processes and (b) assessment of impact evaluation report on capacity of VNRMCs.

title.narrative: Share of Village NRM Committees with equal or more representation of women among 9 members of the Executive Committee

comment.narrative: Almost fully achieved (26%). The indicator measures the proportion of women in community-level decision-making for NRM practices with a target set at 50 percent. At project completion, women participation at executive committees of VNRMCs at 400 project villages was forty-four percent, which equates to 4 four persons out of a group of 9 nine and echoes an instruction given to VNRMC's that at least 4 four out of 9 nine members in each Executive Committee (EC) should be female. Twenty six percent of the VNRMCs had equal or above representation of women in on their ECs.
